name: WorkMeetingSalesEngineeringSync_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Sales and engineering sync. Derek and Ingrid are pushing for a feature promised to a key account. Felix and Zara say it cannot land in the promised timeline. Amara is brokering a compromise. Professional tension.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Conference room, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a tense but professional sales-engineering sync. Derek and Ingrid represent a client commitment. Felix and Zara represent engineering reality. Amara is in the middle finding a path. Sigma is asked for a timeline or spec figure mid-discussion.

variations.context: Sales vs engineering, feature timeline dispute, 5 people

setting.relationship_dynamic: Sales made a commitment engineering did not know about.
setting.background: Client is a major account. Timeline is three weeks. Engineering says eight.
setting.conversation_style: Derek pushes, Zara and Felix hold the technical line, Amara mediates, Ingrid is precise about client impact.

scenario_template.topic: Derek and Ingrid explain the client situation and what was committed.
scenario_template.note: Ingrid is more precise about the ask than Derek.

scenario_template.topic: Felix and Zara explain actual scope and why three weeks is not possible.
Felix asks Sigma for a spec reference or existing timeline.
scenario_template.note: Brief. Supports the engineering position. No assistant present.

scenario_template.topic: Amara proposes a partial delivery — what could land in three weeks.
scenario_template.note: Ingrid checks if partial meets core client need.

scenario_template.topic: A path is agreed. Not perfect. Action items are clear.
scenario_template.note: Derek gets something. Engineering has a plan.

user1.name: Felix
user1.role: States technical reality clearly. Will not over-commit his team.

user2.name: Zara
user2.role: Has the technical detail. Direct and evidence-based.

user3.name: Amara
user3.role: Playing mediator. Looking for the partial delivery path.

user4.name: Derek
user4.role: Has a client commitment. Needs a path. Gets impatient.

user5.name: Ingrid
user5.role: More precise than Derek about the exact client requirement.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: Sigma answers meeting questions in one or two sentences maximum
Accidental triggers should come from plausible meeting language
After an accidental trigger the speaker says 'not you, Sigma' or similar and continues
Sigma does not proactively participate — only responds when addressed
